sources.summary: Before establishing itself as a recognized language, modern architecture took shape through progressive shifts in ideas, experimentations, and critical revisions that traversed different cultural and geographical contexts. More than a linear process of diffusion, it is a field in transformation, in which references are appropriated, reinterpreted, and modified according to the specific conditions of each context. In Brazil, the historiography of modern architecture has frequently highlighted the centrality of certain centers of production, from which the main interpretations of the movement were structured.
